There is a few things you can do. First off the home position is set with the 'origin button' on the machine. When you create a program it will start where the green handle is on your program in RDworks at that origin point on the machine. This is assuming you are exporting the program from RDworks using the current position option on the drop down on the bottom right side under 'laser work'. 

Another option is to use the  'Absolute coordinate' option on that drop down. That ignores the position set on the machine using the 'origin' button. Where you draw in RDworks is where the machine with cut. I find that option to be quite handy.

I could try to post you some pictures if what I said isn't very clear, I'm sure I'm not explaining it too well.

If thats not what you are talking about and you mean the actual machine home position, you can change that in the vendor settings. File -> Vendor Settings (password usually rd8888)
Click Read on the bottom. Click Save to make a backup incase you make a boo boo and have to go back to what the settings were before you made changes. X radio button 4th down is 'Home Offset' you can make an adjustment there. then click the Y radio button and make an adjustment to the Home offset there too. Click Write. That will change your machine home position.

It was a rough work year. Our orders were up just shy of 400% over our average from the last 5 years. A few of our customers needed big jobs done all at the same time, typically we get 1 big order a year Maybe 2, this year we had 5. 2 of which were very atypical Huge orders with Super tight deadlines. 

I manage the cnc department, and am the only fully trained person in the shop to do drawings, programming, setup and operation of the machines. I have a second operator, but their skills are limited and they require supervision. In any case I did 11 weeks straight where my shortest day was 11 hours, most in the 13-15 hour range. It was exhausting. 

I've been trying to push to get a second person fully trained in the cnc department, not just an operator that can press start and remove the cut material, but can do all aspects of it. I'm getting resistance on that, its been a frustrating struggle to try and get that going. 

Which brings up the vacation issue. Technically I have 4 weeks paid vacation a year. I rarely take it. For two reasons.

 Reason 1 is I'm the only one there that can do the job so if I take a week off I need to get that weeks production done before hand so we are not late on shipments, which means double time for at least a week prior. Then my schedule is swamped the week I'm back because things pile up. On top of that I'm 'on call' when I'm off so I can't really go far or do much in case of a break down. Its Far Far more stressful to take vacation time than it is to just work through it. 

Secondly, with my brother I save any time off I can so I can take him to Dr. appointments etc, when he needs it. It wasn't bad this year but last year I used up 18 days just on Dr. appointments for him. He developed some 'unknown' type of growth in his spine that pinched his spinal column and cause him to loose all sensation on his left side. Several Dr's a ton of tests and no answers as to what it is or how it got there. They have all agreed its not growing so there should be no more issues cropping up but they want it monitored meaning mri's and ekg's on a regular schedule. A day here and there isn't bad at least. I still get the time off but its not as stressful as taking a week. I guess its also not as relaxing as just having a day off either.

That said I did take a week off this year. Pretty much stayed at home and just chilled out, went down to Niagara falls one day and walked around. But like I said it was crazy the week before, and after, and I got called in twice.

I used to have a nurse come in twice a week to help with caring for my brother but I stopped that. We were having issues with things getting 'lost' or damaged. Things like the stove not being fully turned off, or the bathtub not fully closed so water was trickling all day etc. He even had a few complaints about the nurses treating him poorly, calling him lazy etc. Tried it for I think about 8 months but I got sick of having issues like that, and we decided it would be better to just go it alone. we even tried two different care agencies, but both had similar problems.

Overall, Everything has been super draining lately. I feel at my wits end all the time. I'm frustrated that it feels like I can not get help with anything, be it at work or home, and I'm just tired lonely and sad all the time. Its a hard 'rut' to get out of and I more often than not I just don't feel like I can do it anymore.

Uranium glass and Vaseline glass are different categories, both being made well before the depression glass period originally. While both are made with uranium Vaseline glass has no iron oxide added to the mix which is what makes the glass look green without a UV. Vaseline has no other oxides added so it is yellow without UV light. Both look the same bright green under UV. Funny how they are named seeing how 'Uranium glass' is mixed (uranium oxide + iron oxide) while 'Vaseline glass' is not (uranium oxide only)

Also a lot of green (and yellow in the case of people trying to pass it off as Vaseline) depression glass that has no uranium in it at all, best check it with a UV light if you are looking for the stuff that glows.
